name: github.com/beevik/etree
scope: XML 1.0 UTF-8 document without DOCTYPE read into an element tree: root and element expanded names in document order, maximum depth, namespace declarations and URIs, non-declaration attributes, decoded character data (predefined entity and character references, CDATA)
family: etree element tree over Go encoding/xml Decoder tokenizer
family_note: etree.go builds its tree from encoding/xml.Decoder.RawToken (strict mode by default) and resolves prefixes itself through Element.NamespaceURI and Attr.NamespaceURI. Lexing, entity and character-reference decoding, and CDATA handling are the standard encoding/xml code, so etree shares the Go encoding/xml Decoder tokenizer family with the unranked standard path; only tree building and namespace lookup are etree's own.

name: github.com/antchfx/xmlquery
input_api: xmlquery.Parse(io.Reader); Node.FirstChild/NextSibling DOM walk; Node.NamespaceURI and Attr.NamespaceURI
scope: XML 1.0 UTF-8 document without DOCTYPE parsed from local io.Reader into a DOM: expanded names, maximum depth, namespace declarations and URIs, attributes, decoded text and CDATA
family: xmlquery DOM over Go encoding/xml Decoder tokenizer
family_note: xmlquery parse.go creates its own Node tree but obtains names, attributes and character data from encoding/xml.Decoder.Token. It shares the Go encoding/xml tokenizer family with etree and the unranked standard path; its DOM construction is separate.

name: github.com/clbanning/mxj
license: MIT, with BSD-3-Clause Go Authors notice
input_api: mxj.NewMapXml([]byte) and mxj.NewMapXmlReader(io.Reader), each returning mxj.Map (map[string]interface{}); the harness requires both maps to agree and walks the map keys
scope: XML 1.0 UTF-8 document without DOCTYPE converted to a map[string]interface{} with default settings: local element names as keys, repeated sibling names as ordered lists, '-'-prefixed attribute keys (namespace declarations included), trimmed decoded character data and CDATA as string values or '#text', and empty elements as empty strings
family: mxj map conversion over Go encoding/xml Decoder tokenizer
family_note: mxj xml.go creates an encoding/xml.Decoder and builds the map itself in xmlToMapParser from Decoder.Token. Lexing, entity and character-reference decoding, CDATA and namespace resolution are the standard encoding/xml code, so mxj shares the Go encoding/xml tokenizer family with etree, xmlquery and the unranked standard path; it is not an independent tokenizer. Only the map construction is mxj's own.
representation_losses: Namespace URIs are dropped: keys use Name.Local only, so c:catalog becomes catalog and p:amount becomes amount.
Namespace prefixes are dropped from element and attribute keys (c:lang becomes -lang).
Namespace declarations are kept only as ordinary attributes named by their local part (xmlns becomes -xmlns, xmlns:c becomes -c); a declaration and an attribute with the same local name collide.
Order between differently named siblings is lost; only same-name siblings keep their relative order in a list.
Comments and processing instructions are discarded.
Mixed content is not preserved: leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed, and multiple text runs in one element overwrite each other in '#text'.

popularity.caveat: Counts importers of the v1 module path github.com/clbanning/mxj only; the separate github.com/clbanning/mxj/v2 path (178) stays an unresolved lead and is not added. Importers may use mxj for JSON or map utilities rather than XML.
